package_info.package_versions: affected versions prior to patches for CVE-2020-15215 and CVE-2020-15174
package_info.why_malicious: The Electron framework, as used in Discord, was configured insecurely (contextIsolation set to false), allowing web content to directly access NodeJS APIs. Combined with a framebusting vulnerability and an XSS on a third-party site, this enabled remote code execution (RCE) on user machines. While Electron itself is not intentionally malicious, these vulnerabilities and misconfigurations allowed attackers to execute arbitrary code, making the package as used in this context effectively malicious.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when user views embedded content in Discord chat)
execution_context.file_location: Electron app main process (Discord Desktop app configuration)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the Electron app disables context isolation, allowing web page JavaScript to access NodeJS APIs directly, enabling arbitrary code execution if malicious JavaScript is loaded.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Disabling context isolation exposes powerful NodeJS APIs to untrusted web content, breaking the security boundary between the renderer and Node context.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, Electron apps should isolate web content from NodeJS APIs to prevent untrusted code from executing system-level actions. Here, the boundary is removed.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legacy Electron apps may disable context isolation for compatibility, but this is strongly discouraged.
key_indicators: NodeJS APIs accessible from web content

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when user clicks embedded iframe in Discord chat)
execution_context.file_location: Electron renderer process (embedded iframe from SketchFab)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: window.top.location = malicious_url; // framebusting to escape iframe
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, malicious JavaScript in an embedded iframe uses framebusting to break out of the iframe and execute in the top frame, bypassing intended isolation and gaining access to the Electron/NodeJS context.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Framebusting is used to escape the security sandbox of an iframe, allowing untrusted content to interact with the main application context.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Embedded content should remain sandboxed and not be able to affect the parent application frame.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Framebusting is sometimes used for legitimate navigation, but not in the context of embedded third-party content in a desktop app.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when malicious payload is loaded via XSS on SketchFab)
execution_context.file_location: Electron renderer process (malicious JavaScript loaded from SketchFab)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, malicious JavaScript loaded via XSS exploits the lack of context isolation to invoke NodeJS child_process.exec, executing arbitrary system commands (e.g., launching calculator or running malware).

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Web content should never be able to execute system commands. This is a direct path to remote code execution.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal web content in Electron should not have access to NodeJS process APIs, especially for command execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate Electron apps may use child_process for internal features, but never exposed to untrusted web content.
key_indicators: Execution of system commands from web content

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts a malicious payload exploiting XSS on SketchFab and hosts it on the site.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious payload is available for embedding.

attack_chain.action: Attacker shares the malicious SketchFab URL in Discord chat, which Discord embeds as an iframe.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious iframe is loaded in Discord's Electron app.

attack_chain.action: User clicks the embedded iframe, triggering framebusting code to escape the iframe and execute in the top frame.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code now runs in the main Electron renderer context.

attack_chain.action: Due to contextIsolation: false, malicious JavaScript gains access to NodeJS APIs and executes arbitrary system commands.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution on the user's machine (final goal).

behavioral_signatures: Electron apps with contextIsolation set to false
Renderer process accessing NodeJS APIs (e.g., require('child_process'))
Framebusting attempts from embedded iframes (window.top.location assignment)
Execution of system commands from web content context
file_indicators: Electron app configuration with contextIsolation: false
Presence of embedded iframes loading third-party content (e.g., SketchFab) in chat windows
network_indicators: Loading of external content from domains with known XSS vulnerabilities (e.g., sketchfab.com)
Unexpected outbound connections initiated by the Electron renderer process
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Electron app configurations for insecure settings (contextIsolation: false). Detect renderer processes attempting to access NodeJS APIs or execute system commands. Watch for framebusting behavior in embedded iframes and for loading of third-party content from domains with known vulnerabilities. Alert on any web content in the renderer process invoking require('child_process') or similar APIs.
